name: Kath Breaks Up with Carl Outside Rudy's
description: On New Year's Eve, Carl and Kath stand outside Rudy's bar, where a steady stream of people pass by on their way into the celebration. Kath tells Carl he has stopped doing anything with his life, saying he used to be fun and had dreams of business school and working for the World Bank. Carl responds that he simply changed his mind about business school, calling it personal growth. Kath argues that growth means moving to something new, not withdrawing from life. She expresses frustration that he isn’t upset about the breakup, saying he should be angry or sad. Carl says he understands they’re in different places. Kath insists it’s okay for him to be angry, even to call her a name, but Carl says that would be inappropriate. As tears form in her eyes, she says she can’t believe she’s been with someone so emotionless. Carl steps forward and hugs her, telling her it will be okay.

name: Kath Breaks Up with Carl at Rudy's on New Year's Eve
description: Kath and Carl stand outside Rudy's bar on New Year's Eve, surrounded by people arriving for the celebration. Kath tells Carl he has changed, that he used to be fun and have dreams, but now he does nothing and stays in his apartment. Carl replies that he's there, isn't he? Kath says being at the bar only because it's New Year's Eve proves her point. She reminds him he once wanted to go to business school, wanted to work for the World Bank. Carl says he realized business school wasn't for him, and people change. Kath argues that change means moving to something new, not giving up and sitting on the couch. Carl agrees it's been hard, and he understands her point. Kath says that's the problem—he doesn't seem to care that she's breaking up with him. Carl says he does care, but he understands. Kath insists he should be mad, sad, upset—anything but calm. Carl says they're in different places. Kath says it's not right that he just accepts it, that he won't even call her a bitch. Carl says that would be inappropriate. Kath starts to cry, saying she can't believe she's been with someone so emotionless. Carl steps forward and hugs her. She doesn't pull away.

He asks Carl if he’s back for more, then follows up by saying he’s out of cash and wonders if Carl can cover drinks for him and his buddies, pointing to four people sitting at the bar. Peter says he didn’t bring his wallet. Carl hesitates, then says yes. He walks up to the bar, turns to the group, and asks what kind of beer they want. Rooney’s friends respond with extravagant requests—Grey Goose straight up, Kir Royale, and whatever’s in the dusty bottle behind the bar that never gets taken down.

They walk into the bank together. Chris greets Norman Calhoun, introducing himself as the new president of Southwest Bank and saying he’s visiting each branch to meet the managers. He turns briefly to Carl, who mentions he’s just a teller. Chris replies that he was once just a teller too, now president of the largest bank in the Southwest. He tells Norman to reach out to corporate if needed. After they leave, Norman remarks on Parker’s success, and Carl mutters a comment about fake breasts and German engineering. The bank customer returns, asking for help, and Carl directs them to Norman.

name: Carl's Repetitive Day Unfolds
description: Carl lies down. The alarm goes off. Quick cuts show Carl at Dunkin Donuts, turning down a pamphlet. He walks down the street. Inside Southwest Bank, Norman speaks to him, suggesting he dress as his favorite animal. Carl shakes his head. The clock flips to 5:00. At home, Carl eats frozen lasagna while watching The Amazing Race. The images grow faster. Carl is back at Dunkin Donuts. He returns to the bank, Norman talking to him again, this time mentioning a historical figure. Carl says no. The clock flips to 5:00. Carl eats frozen meatloaf, watching Project Runway. His head hits the pillow. He wakes up. He shakes his head. The clock flips to 5:00. His head hits the bed again. The alarm sounds. The scenes blur—Carl at the bank, refusing, eating Lean Cuisine, watching television, the clock striking 5:00, over and over.

name: Carl and Alex Reunite at the Picnic Table
description: Carl is eating lunch at a picnic table outside when Alex approaches him. Alex calls out Carl's name, and Carl recognizes him, responding with surprise. Alex hugs Carl without hesitation. They exchange greetings, and Alex speaks excitedly about where he's been. He says he climbed Mount Kilimanjaro, ate bat in Laos, and shot a cow with a bazooka. Carl tells Alex the bank is the same as always. Alex says that's the problem—that people waste their lives on routine. He hands Carl a pamphlet for a 'Just Say Yes' seminar and insists it changed his life. Carl jokes that he sometimes wants to throw rocks at the bank, and Alex immediately starts doing it. Carl tells him to stop, saying he was only joking. Norman comes outside, recognizes Alex, and asks if it's a prank. Alex keeps throwing rocks. Norman speaks into a walkie-talkie, and two portly security guards come out, tackle Alex, and try to hold him down. Alex breaks free and runs away, shouting to Carl to attend the seminar.

Carl replies that he doesn’t want an adventure first thing in the morning. The waitress arrives and starts going over the specials. She mentions a double fruit burnt sugar waffle. Carl says yes. She then describes a smoked whitefish omelet with hash browns. Carl says yes. The waitress, surprised, confirms he wants both. He does. She asks if he wants toast. He says yes. She lists bacon as a side. He says yes. She mentions sausage. He says yes. Turkey sausage. He says yes. She brings up a side of maple pancakes. He says yes. She remarks that someone is really hungry. Carl says yes. She asks if he wants coffee or juice. He says coffee and juice. She adds that they have smoothies. He says yes. The others at the table stare at him. The waitress, relieved, asks if that’s all. Carl says yes. She turns to the others and asks what they would like to order. They continue to look at Carl.

name: Peter Confronts Carl About His Isolation
description: Peter arrives at Carl's apartment and tells him he's there for an intervention, pointing out that Carl missed their engagement party. Carl brushes it off, saying he’s busy and might need to wake up early. Peter counters that Carl is watching Hell's Kitchen and mocks the show as low-tier reality TV. He brings up that it’s been over a year since Carl broke up with Kath and he still hasn’t dated anyone. Carl jokes that he’s like a camel, only needing romance every few years. Peter insists it’s more serious, comparing Carl to someone still wearing a Timex while everyone else has moved on to Rolexes. Carl asks if Peter actually owns a Rolex, and Peter confirms it’s an Oyster Perpetual Yachtmaster, worth four thousand dollars. Carl dismisses it, saying he doesn’t care about watches or his friends’ obsession with real estate and Crate and Barrel. Peter replies that Carl never leaves his apartment or meets new people, calling him a cave dweller. Carl defends himself by recalling the time he stole a drumstick from a band backstage at Summerfest. Peter tells him that happened seven years ago. Carl is stunned, realizing he’s been working at Southwest Bank for ten years. He does the math aloud, saying a child born then would be toilet-trained, but Peter corrects him—fourth grade. Carl insists he was already grown by fourth grade, then snaps, telling Peter he’s an adult and can live how he wants. He pushes Peter out the door. Alone, Carl sits on the couch and unfolds a crumpled 'Just Say Yes' pamphlet, revealing a smiling Indian man on the cover.

Peter mentions his Oakleys, saying they make the wait easier. Carl steps forward and tells the waitress they were there before the Lowell party. She replies that they weren’t, pointing to her list. Carl insists they were, and the waitress repeats that the list doesn’t lie. Carl retorts that this time it did. Lucy tries to calm him, saying it’s just brunch. Carl turns to the departing customers and declares they all know his group was there first, and they’ll have to live with that. Peter pulls Carl back. name: Carl Arrives at Sanji's Lecture and Keeps His Distance
description: Carl enters the conference room and takes a seat beside a wiry, crunchy woman. She asks if it’s his first time at one of Sanji’s lectures. Around him, people settle into their seats. Carl remains in the back. A voice echoes over the sound system—Sanji’s—asking what life really is and where consciousness begins. Carl laughs quietly. No one else does. The lights shift to a soft rose hue as Sanji’s voice continues, speaking about change, consciousness, and choice.

Sanji raises his fist and shouts 'Yes!' The crowd echoes him. 'Say yes! For your life! Yes! Change starts now!' he calls, leading a loud, rhythmic chant. The crowd responds in unison, shouting 'Yes!' with each prompt. Indoor fireworks pop and flash as Sanji moves through the audience, feeding off the growing energy.
